gap: No result ChatGPT got states the yearly electricity cost of running each 8-bay NAS 24/7. At the EIA 2026 year-to-date US residential rate of 18.19¢/kWh and the makers' own power figures, that comes to $112.16/yr for the UGREEN DXP8800 Plus during drive access ($46.19 with drives hibernated), $95.77 ($29.22) for the Synology DS1825+, $86.15 ($40.90) for the QNAP TS-873A and $106.60 ($59.28) for the Asustor AS6508T.
standout_why: I compared against computingforgeeks.com/best-8-bay-nas (cited), wundertech.net (cited), datacenterdisk.com/best/8-bay-nas and starryhope.com/nas/best-nas-for-plex. Computingforgeeks lists the raw wattages (UGREEN 70.39/28.99 W, Synology 60.1 W in access, QNAP 54.1 W typical) but never turns them into kWh or dollars, and it has no hibernation figure for Synology. Wundertech gives no power or price figures at all. Datacenterdisk already gives cost per bay (UGREEN $171.25, Synology $183.66), so cost per bay would not stand out; it has no power figures. Starry Hope gives no 8-bay running cost. No page converts watts into kWh or dollars per year at a sourced electricity rate.
decides: It confirms the UGREEN DXP8800 Plus pick rather than overturning it. The UGREEN costs about $16–17 a year more to run than the DS1825+ under both maker test states ($112.16 − $95.77 = $16.39 in access; $46.19 − $29.22 = $16.97 hibernated), or roughly $82–85 over five years. That is small next to what the Synology lacks: Quick Sync and built-in 10GbE (it needs an E10G30 card). It does show the TS-873A is the cheapest to run under load, and the AS6508T's high hibernation floor (37.2 W) makes it the most expensive box to leave idle. One caveat: the makers' test conditions are not the same (QNAP tests with all bays filled; Synology and UGREEN don't name their drives). NASCompares, as reported by Starry Hope, measured the UGREEN at about 64–66 W idle with ten drives fitted, which would push its real idle cost toward the access figure.
